concepts.why: The presence of a focal hypoechoic polypoidal lesion and a well-defined soft-tissue–density lesion with calcific specks along the anterosuperior bladder wall, as well as heterogeneous enhancement in the early arterial and venous phases, are highly suggestive of bladder cancer.

The presence of a focal hypoechoic polypoidal lesion and an indistinct outline of the adjacent bladder wall, combined with the patient's history of abdominal hysterectomy and the presence of left hydrosalpinx, suggest the possibility of bladder endometriosis.
The presence of tiny hyperechoic foci and a well-defined soft-tissue–density lesion with calcific specks along the anterosuperior bladder wall are consistent with malacoplakia of the urinary bladder.
The presence of a right calyceal calculus with mild pelvicalyceal dilatation is diagnostic of nephrolithiasis.
The presence of a simple right renal cyst is a common finding and may be unrelated to the patient's symptoms.

frontier_selector.rationale: The presence of a focal hypoechoic polypoidal lesion and a well-defined soft-tissue–density lesion with calcific specks along the anterosuperior bladder wall, demonstrating heterogeneous enhancement, strongly supports Urinary Bladder Cancer. While Urinary Bladder Endometriosis is a consideration due to the patient's history and the presence of a left hydrosalpinx, the imaging findings more specifically align with cancer.
